meta.title: MCP tool ontology - servers, tool groups, broad categories
meta.frame: Broad-category routing map of every MCP server/connector available to Claude Code on this machine. Nodes: category (what a tool is for), server, tool_group (a server's tool namespace, with its tools listed). Relations: provides, in_category, overlaps_with (interchangeable/duplicate tool groups - the routing ambiguity), feeds (category-level workflow). Not an ontology/ financial graph: it does not use taxonomy.json. bounded_contexts: one entry per MCP server (the server:<name> node), stating what it owns and where its boundary is - the single source for server descriptions.
meta.source: tool names from the session's tool list; tool_group.tools is abridged, not exhaustive. Regenerate via live tools/list introspection for exact schemas.
meta.often_follows_source: ~/.claude/claude_hooks.sqlite hook_logs `PTU enter` lines; regenerate with scripts/mine_tool_sequences.py

bounded_contexts.claude-code: Claude Code's own built-in tools, not an MCP server: shell and file editing, web search/fetch, subagent orchestration, and tool/skill discovery. Owns the act of working in the current workspace; it has no domain data of its own and every other context is reached through it.
bounded_contexts.claude-hooks: This repo's local server: the memory store (MEMORY.sqlite, tool hints), code and diff RAG indexes, a scratch key-value store, a reasoning aid, and the hook/session observability tools (logs, checkpoints, server memory). Owns what the agent remembers and what happened in past sessions; it does not own tasks.
bounded_contexts.taskfw: The task-framework server: task lifecycle (create, groom, implement, finish, introspect), decisions and commits per task, task-scoped memory, and the concept store of architectural facts. Owns why work was done and what each module promises; claude-hooks depends on it, never the reverse.
bounded_contexts.local-mac: The user's own Mac reached through one Swift binary: Obsidian vault and its RAG, Apple Notes/Calendar/Reminders/Contacts/Mail/iMessage, Safari, system state and devices (power, sound, VPN, music, podcasts, time), a code RAG, local-model delegation and gold-regime market data. Owns local personal data and device control; hosted equivalents live in the claude_ai_* connectors.
bounded_contexts.wyckoff-analyzer: Indian equity analysis: Wyckoff accumulation/spring/SOS detection, support and resistance, sector relative strength, momentum portfolio rebalance and exit checks, plus the data-refresh steps (delivery, F&O, short volume, run state) that feed them. Owns market-signal computation; it does not fetch pages itself, so scraped data arrives via ui_automation.
bounded_contexts.astrology: Vedic astrology queries against the user's chart: planets and lagna, dasha and pratyantar timelines, divisional charts, yogas, gochar transits and panchang. Owns chart and timing computation; it interprets nothing outside astrology.
bounded_contexts.sysml-mcp: SysML v2 modelling: parse and validate model text or files, symbol/definition/reference/hierarchy queries, complexity metrics and diagram preview. Owns the structural model under models/*.sysml; it renders diagrams but does not decide what the model should say.
bounded_contexts.claude-in-chrome: Chrome driven through the browser extension: tabs, navigation, page reads, form input, page JavaScript, console/network inspection and GIF recording. Owns DOM-level browser automation in Chrome; Safari lives in local-mac and pixel-level control in computer-use.
bounded_contexts.computer-use: Foreground, pixel-level desktop control: screenshots, clicks, typing, scrolling, dragging, opening apps and the clipboard, gated by per-app access. Owns anything with no DOM or accessibility handle; it blocks input to browsers, which is why browser work goes to Safari or Chrome instead.
bounded_contexts.cmux-cua: Background, accessibility-tree driven app control that does not steal focus or move the cursor: launch apps, read window state, click/type by element index, record sessions. Owns unattended native-app automation; the foreground alternative is computer-use.
bounded_contexts.claude_ai_Claude_Docs: Hosted living documents that people share, comment on and edit: create, read, update, delete, query, batch edit, export. Owns collaborative documents in the claude.ai account; the local vault is a separate store for the user's own notes.
bounded_contexts.claude_ai_Google_Drive: Google Drive files: search, read, download, create, update, copy, trash, share, metadata, permissions and recent files. Owns hosted files and their sharing; nothing here is a note or a document in the Claude Docs sense.
bounded_contexts.claude_ai_Notion: Notion workspace pages, reached through an authenticated connector. Only the authenticate/complete_authentication tools are listed here, so its boundary is 'Notion content once signed in'; local Obsidian notes are the alternative.
bounded_contexts.claude_ai_Slack: Slack workspace messaging, reached through an authenticated connector. Only the authenticate/complete_authentication tools are listed here, so its boundary is 'Slack channels and threads once signed in'.
bounded_contexts.claude_ai_Gmail: Gmail mail, reached through an authenticated connector. Only the authenticate/complete_authentication tools are listed here; Apple Mail in local-mac is the local alternative and the two overlap.
bounded_contexts.claude_ai_Google_Calendar: Google Calendar events, reached through an authenticated connector. Only the authenticate/complete_authentication tools are listed here; Apple Calendar in local-mac is the local alternative and the two overlap.

relation_types.in_category: tool group serves this broad purpose
relation_types.overlaps_with: two tool groups can do the same job - choose by constraint
relation_types.feeds: output of source category is typically input to target category
relation_types.often_follows: mined from PostToolUse `PTU enter` log lines: target is called next after source within one session (count; p = share of the source's successors)
relation_types.member_of: tool belongs to the tool group
relation_types.intercepts: hook event runs on every call in the target scope, before (PreToolUse) or after (PostToolUse) it
